questions.scenario: It is School Cabinet Election time! How do you help your best friend win the 'Head Boy/Girl' title?

options.text: Analyze past voting trends to figure out exactly which class sections to target for maximum votes.
Write a highly emotional, catchy speech and spread viral WhatsApp slogans to build massive hype.
Make the core campaign promise about improving the hygiene of the school canteen for everyone's health.
Map out the exact locations in the school corridors where campaign posters will get the most eyeballs.

questions.scenario: There is a massive, honking traffic jam outside your school gate every single morning. How do you solve it?

options.text: Calculate the average delay time and draft a logical proposal to stagger school timings by 15 minutes.
Convince the local traffic inspector to visit the school, ensuring they see the chaos and deploy a constable.
Start a neighborhood 'Carpool or Walk' initiative among parents to reduce the carbon footprint.
Sketch a new one-way drop-off lane blueprint that prevents auto-rickshaws from blocking the main road.

questions.scenario: A garbage dump is piling up near your colony's park, and the WhatsApp uncle-aunty group is panicking. Your move?

options.text: Research the Municipal Corporation's solid waste rules and file a formal, fact-checked grievance online.
Rally all the angry residents and build a strong pressure group to force the RWA President to act.
Organize a Sunday morning 'Clean-Up Drive' with your friends and provide gloves to the local ragpickers.
Design a permanent, color-coded bin system for the society, placed exactly 50 meters apart for easy access.

questions.scenario: The school principal announces a total ban on bringing mobile phones, even for students traveling far. Your reaction?

options.text: Look up CBSE guidelines and propose a 'deposit at the gate' policy based on actual safety statistics.
Start a massive signature campaign among the senior students to forcefully negotiate the rule.
Argue that the ban is unfair to students who travel by public bus and genuinely need phones for safety.
Suggest installing a secure, numbered locker system at the main reception to manage the phones efficiently.

questions.scenario: Diwali pollution is getting out of hand, and the city's AQI is touching 500. What's your approach to the problem?

options.text: Read the actual data comparing the impact of firecrackers versus stubble burning to understand the real root cause.
Run a highly persuasive social media campaign making it 'uncool' for teenagers to burst noisy crackers.
Distribute N95 masks to local street food vendors and auto-drivers who cannot afford to stay indoors.
Propose a central society ground for a unified laser show, preventing individual smoke clusters in the colony.

questions.scenario: You are given Rs. 10,000 to manage the society's Ganesh Chaturthi / Durga Puja festival. What do you do?

options.text: Create a strict Excel sheet allocating exact funds for the pandal, prasad, and music to avoid overspending.
Use part of the money to invite the local MLA as a VIP guest to secure better society funding for next year.
Donate 30% of the budget to a nearby orphanage and keep the society's decorations beautifully simple.
Invest in a proper eco-friendly immersion tank setup and sturdy barricades to manage the crowd flow.

questions.scenario: The famous 'Khau Galli' (street food lane) near your tuition is being shut down by the authorities for blocking traffic. Your stance?

options.text: Analyze the municipal zoning laws and draft a report on how vendors can legally comply to stay open.
Help the momo and chaat walas form a union to protest and gain the support of the local corporator.
Start a crowdfunding page to help the poorest vendors upgrade to licensed, hygienic food carts.
Redraw the street map to show how carts can be parked in an organized line without choking the traffic.

questions.scenario: Stray dogs in the colony are a hot topic of argument on the family WhatsApp group. How do you step in?

options.text: Post the official Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI) guidelines to shut down the fake rumors with facts.
Identify the loudest complainers in the group and privately convince them to calm down and compromise.
Partner with a local animal rescue NGO to organize a vaccination, neutering, and feeding drive.
Identify an unused plot behind the society and propose fencing it to create a designated, safe 'dog zone'.

questions.scenario: You are visiting a crowded historical monument (like Qutub Minar, Charminar, or Taj Mahal). What naturally interests you?

options.text: Reading the information boards to understand the economic history and preservation cost of the site.
Convincing the strict security guard with a big smile to let your group carry your DSLR camera inside.
Buying handicrafts directly from the local artisans outside the gate to support their livelihood.
Observing how brilliantly the pathways, ticket counters, and exit gates handle thousands of tourists.

questions.scenario: During a massive power cut (load shedding) in peak summer, how do you keep your cool?

options.text: Check the electricity board's official schedule and calculate exactly when the power grid will be restored.
Keep the family's mood light by telling funny stories and completely distracting them from the heat.
Check on the elderly neighbors to make sure they have enough battery-operated fans and drinking water.
Figure out the most cross-ventilated room in the house and make everyone sit there to catch the breeze.

Policy_Analyst.title: The Data Detective (Policy Analyst / Think Tank Researcher)
Policy_Analyst.primary_match_text: You are highly analytical, rely on hard facts, and love solving big problems. You don't just complain about the system; you research how to fix it.
Policy_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Working with government bodies like NITI Aayog, reading reports, analyzing national data, and writing policies that impact millions of Indians.
Policy_Analyst.alternative_match_text: If not public policy, your analytical brain would be fantastic in Economics, Data Science, or Corporate Strategy.
Policy_Analyst.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Humanities or Commerce (with Math/Economics). Degree: BA in Economics, Political Science, or Statistics. Next Steps: Pursue a Master's in Public Policy (MPP) from top institutes like NLSIU, TISS, or Ashoka University.

Political_Strategist.title: The Mastermind (Political Strategist / Campaign Manager)
Political_Strategist.primary_match_text: You understand human psychology perfectly. You are persuasive, a great communicator, and know exactly how to influence crowds and win people over.
Political_Strategist.day_in_the_life: Working behind the scenes for major Indian elections, managing politicians' social media, analyzing voter sentiment, and creating viral campaign slogans.
Political_Strategist.alternative_match_text: With your massive influence skills, you would also excel in Public Relations (PR), Marketing, or Media Management.
Political_Strategist.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (Humanities is great). Degree: BA in Political Science, Journalism, or Mass Communication. Next Steps: Work with political consulting firms like I-PAC or join a media agency.

Social_Entrepreneur.title: The Changemaker (Social Entrepreneur / NGO Founder)
Social_Entrepreneur.primary_match_text: You have a massive heart and a strong drive to help others. You cannot sit and watch injustice happen—you take action at the grassroots level.
Social_Entrepreneur.day_in_the_life: Traveling to rural India, setting up educational programs for underprivileged kids, running NGOs, and solving massive social issues on the ground.
Social_Entrepreneur.alternative_match_text: Your high empathy and leadership make you a great fit for Human Resources (HR), Teaching, or Psychology.
Social_Entrepreneur.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream. Degree: Bachelor of Social Work (BSW), BA in Sociology, or BBA. Next Steps: Pursue an MSW from TISS or take up fellowships like the Gandhi Fellowship or Teach for India.

Urban_Planner.title: The City Architect (Urban Planner / Smart City Developer)
Urban_Planner.primary_match_text: You think in systems, structures, and designs. You love optimizing spaces and making things function smoothly for large groups of people.
Urban_Planner.day_in_the_life: Designing blueprints for India's upcoming 'Smart Cities', planning metro routes, solving massive traffic problems, and making cities eco-friendly.
Urban_Planner.alternative_match_text: Your spatial logic and design skills would also make you a brilliant Architect, Civil Engineer, or Supply Chain Manager.
Urban_Planner.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCM is usually required). Degree: Bachelor of Planning (B.Plan) or Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch). Next Steps: Master's in Urban Planning from SPA (School of Planning and Architecture) or CEPT.
